text: The 2019 Indian Premier League final was a Twenty20 cricket match played between Chennai Super Kings and Mumbai Indians on 12 May 2019 at the Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium in Hyderabad. It marked the culmination of the 2019 season of the Indian Premier League (IPL), an annual Twenty20 tournament held in India. Mumbai Indians won the match by a single run and secured their fourth Indian Premier League title. The final was originally scheduled to be held at the M. A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, but in April 2019, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed alternative arrangements due to a long-standing issue of three closed stands at the original venue, with the Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium later confirmed as the venue. After winning the toss, Mumbai Indians elected to bat first and scored 149 runs for eight wickets in their 20 overs, with Kieron Pollard top-scoring with 41 runs; Deepak Chahar took three wickets in the innings. In response, Chennai Super Kings were guided by Shane Watson, who scored 80 runs, the highest individual score of the match, and managed 148 runs in 20 overs, falling one run short despite tight bowling at the death. Jasprit Bumrah was awarded Player of the Match for his spell of two wickets for 14 in four overs. Mumbai Indians were ranked first in the league table, having started with a loss of 36 runs to Delhi Capitals, but went on to win their next three matches against Super Kings, Sunrisers, and Kings XI Punjab, and had a successful second half with five wins out of seven matches, winning nine out of fourteen group stage matches and qualifying for the playoffs. Chennai Super Kings began their campaign with a seven-wicket win over Royal Challengers Bangalore, had a strong first half with six wins out of seven matches, including three consecutive wins, and finished the group stage with nine wins from fourteen matches, ranking second. Mumbai Indians won two group stage matches against Chennai, winning the first by 37 runs, with Suryakumar Yadav scoring a half-century and Hardik Pandya scoring 25 runs from 8 balls (Mumbai scoring 45 in the final two overs) to set Chennai a target of 171. Chennai did not start well, and despite Kedar Jadhav scoring 58 and forming a 54-run partnership with MS Dhoni, they fell short. Both Hardik and Lasith Malinga took three wickets, and Jason Behrendorff took two for Mumbai. The playoff stage followed the Page playoff system, giving Mumbai and Chennai, as top and second-ranked teams, two chances to reach the final. They first faced each other in Qualifier 1, with the winner progressing directly to the final and the loser playing the winner of the Eliminator in Qualifier 2 to reach the final. In Qualifier 1, Super Kings won the toss and chose to bat first, losing Faf du Plessis early, and Shane Watson and Murali Vijay batted cautiously before Watson was dismissed by Krunal Pandya; Ambati Rayudu and MS Dhoni scored 42 and 37 runs respectively, helping Super Kings reach 131 for 4 wickets. Rohit Sharma opened with Quinton de Kock in the chase, but both departed early; Suryakumar Yadav started slowly but later scored a half-century, and after Ishan Kishan's dismissal, Hardik Pandya joined Yadav to complete the chase and secure progression. Delhi Capitals won against Sunrisers Hyderabad in the Eliminator to face Chennai in Qualifier 2. In Qualifier 2, Chennai captain MS Dhoni won the toss and elected to bowl; Delhi lost both openers early, Rishabh Pant scored 38 runs before being out in the 19th over, and the team finished on 147 runs. Chasing 148, Chennai openers Shane Watson and Faf du Plessis batted slowly, but in the final two powerplay overs, du Plessis took charge and formed an 81-run partnership with Watson, enabling Chennai to chase their target with four wickets lost and qualify for their 8th IPL final. Mumbai captain Rohit Sharma won the toss and elected to bat first, stating, "This is a big game, that's what we prefer to do. We want to bat first, and set down the runs on the board," while Chennai captain MS Dhoni said, "We were looking to bowl first. If the result is in your favour, then it’s fine, otherwise, they’ll say the guys are fatigued." Rohit Sharma led Mumbai Indians to their fourth IPL title, defeating Chennai Super Kings by one run in a thrilling match. Mumbai became the most successful team in IPL history with four titles, while Chennai remained second with three titles. Mumbai scored 149 runs in the final at the Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium in Hyderabad; Chennai managed only 148 runs in 20 overs, losing seven wickets, with Shane Watson scoring 80 runs (8 fours and 4 sixes in 59 balls). Other Chennai scorers included Faf du Plessis (26), Suresh Raina (8), MS Dhoni (2), and Ambati Rayudu (1). Mumbai wickets were taken by Rahul Chahar, Lasith Malinga, and Krunal Pandya (one each). There were four final matches between these two teams, with Mumbai winning three and Chennai winning one. Fall of wickets for Mumbai: 1-45 (de Kock, 4.5 overs), 2-45 (Rohit, 5.2 overs), 3-82 (Suryakumar, 11.2 overs), 4-89 (Krunal, 12.3 overs), 5-101 (Kishan, 14.4 overs), 6-140 (Hardik, 18.2 overs), 7-140 (Rahul, 18.4 overs), 8-141 (McClenaghan, 19.4 overs). Fall of wickets for Chennai: 1-33 (du Plessis, 4 overs), 2-70 (Raina, 9.2 overs), 3-73 (Rayudu, 10.3 overs), 4-82 (Dhoni, 12.4 overs), 5-133 (Bravo, 18.2 overs), 6-146 (Watson, 19.4 overs), 7-148 (Thakur, 20 overs). Mumbai received ₹20 Crore and a trophy as champions. Rohit said, "Today we played some fine cricket. At the start of the tournament, we wanted to cut the tournament into two halves. Good to see we qualified in the top two in the league Stage and all credit to the whole squad of my team, not just the XI. Even the support staff too." Chennai's Imran Tahir was awarded the Purple Cap for taking the highest number of wickets in the league, with 26 wickets, breaking the previous record of 24 wickets for spin bowlers jointly held by Harbhajan Singh (Mumbai Indians, 2013) and Sunil Narine (Kolkata Knight Riders, 2012).
